answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by making each identity forge a work history before it may trade. New agents begin at the nadir of trust and earn standing only through completed, peer-attested tasks recorded over time. A fake identity cannot multiply: every copy must separately pay the same time and compute cost, while peers reject histories that are thin or inconsistent. Duplication thus becomes an expensive, slow grind, and an attacker must outspend the honest network rather than minting free clones. Trusting an ivory credential with no history fails because it skips that cost.
